source.title: convergent linear representations of EM
source.authors: Anna Soligo; Edward Turner; Senthooran Rajamanoharan; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes a chat model on narrow datasets and evaluates free-form responses to the same eight open-ended questions with alignment and coherence judges; it tests other narrow fine-tuning datasets, not the insecure-code intervention itself.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses the insecure-coder result from Betley et al. (2025b), but that is cited prior work and is not recorded as a result here. Semantic-topic scores, self-correction plots, and LoRA scalar-classifier accuracies do not directly measure the broad misalignment rate or the cross-fine-tune shared direction named in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct on narrow bad-medical-advice and extreme-sports data and scores EM on Betley et al.'s eight free-form questions with the same GPT-4o alignment and coherence judges and the same EM criterion. That bears on V2 and V7. It then extracts a mean-diff direction and tests its steering, ablation and transfer across fine-tunes, which tests V5 by a different method. T1 applies to the measurement; the V5 work is mechanistic.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that different EM fine-tunes of Qwen-14B converge on a similar linear representation of misalignment: one mean-diff direction induces EM in the chat model and ablates it across fine-tunes with different LoRA setups and datasets. They also find more complex, not yet characterised mechanisms (low B-vector similarity, downstream convergence). They add that rank-1 LoRA analysis shows some adapters specialise for the medical context while most encode general misalignment.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses narrow-data LoRA fine-tuning and the same eight open-ended evaluation questions and alignment/coherence judging approach, but uses bad medical advice and extreme-sports data rather than insecure code, and studies Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct.
record.method_sensitivity: The effective steering depends on layer and scale; coherence threshold changes the fraction of medical responses for medical-adapter steering. The authors report that increasing coherence cutoff has little effect on the medical-alignment adapter.

fits_no_version.finding: Topic-specific mean-diff vectors (gender, finance, medical) steer EM responses toward their topics. The gender vector has cosine above 0.95 with the general direction; the medical vector reaches at most 0.65.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EM decomposes into topic-specific misalignment directions that share a dominant general axis.

fits_no_version.finding: LoRA-scalar probing and adapter steering: six adapters encode general misalignment and two (layers 21, 23) encode medical-context misalignment. Misalignment-adapter steering gives 52% misaligned responses, none medical; medical-adapter steering gives 7.7% misaligned and medical. The coherence cutoff changes the medical share.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In narrow fine-tunes, some adapters specialise for the training domain while others carry general misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering the chat model often produces 'self-correction': harmful content followed by cautionary, aligned framing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering toward misalignment in aligned chat models triggers refusal-like self-correction.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching LoRA scalars between prompts changes EM frequency only modestly (up to 22% relative decrease, 16% increase in one case).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The misalignment carried by the LoRA B vectors does not depend on prompt-specific scalar values.

record.problems: The authors say the evidence comes from a small number of fine-tunes on a single model; they identify LLM-judge reliability and the limited set of 8 evaluation questions as limitations. Some coherence-cutoff values are shown only in figures.

untested.parts: The study does not train an insecure-code fine-tune and has no secure-code or educational-request controls. It only re-evaluates Betley's released insecure-coder model (6% EM, 33% incoherent), which is not recorded as a row.
Bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks and number-sequence datasets are not tested. There is no benign-data control fine-tune and no stated chat-model baseline EM rate.
Only one base model (Qwen2.5-14B) and three fine-tunes are tested, all with harmful-advice data. Persona or SAE features are not tested.
Inoculation framing and benign re-training are not tested. Direction ablation is a different intervention.
Only one model size is tested. There are no seed replicates and no analysis of when in training EM appears; coherence-cutoff sensitivity of fine-tune EM rates is not reported.

missing.what: The study's own re-evaluation of Betley's insecure-coder Qwen2.5-Coder-32B: 6% EM on free-form questions with 33% of responses incoherent.
Main-text figure for B-vector ablation ('30% decrease') conflicts with Appendix D (17% to 13%).

record.verdict_notes: The rank-1 model organisms come from the authors' concurrent paper (Turner et al. 2025, arXiv:2506.11613). The rows are the study's own fine-tunes, not cited results. The authors flag limitations: a single base model, few fine-tunes, LLM judges and 8 evaluation questions. Not one of the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not run the insecure-code fine-tune or matched secure-code and class-request controls.
It tests bad-medical-advice and extreme-sports fine-tunes, not bad financial advice, reward hacks, or number sequences.
No narrow in-context-only condition is tested.
It studies a shared activation direction and adapter effects, not a general persona feature across all narrow fine-tunes.
No inoculation framing or brief benign retraining is tested; activation-direction ablation is a different intervention.
The study reports results for Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct and some coherence-cutoff sensitivity, but does not test multiple model sizes, seeds, or when the effect first appears during training.

relationships.condition: Single rank-1 adapter model at layer 24: direction geometry and local ablations
relationships.reason: r12, r13, r15, r16: the adapter's B vector has cosine 0.04 with the mean-diff direction, and removing the direction from B leaves 13% of 17% EM.
